Oil Prices Decline After Draft of Iran Peace Agreement Circulates
Source: United Press International (syndicated on Yahoo Finance) | Author: Joe Fisher | Monday 2 November 2026, 4:29 p.m. GMT

Crude oil prices fell significantly on Monday following the circulation of a draft peace agreement between the United States and Iran.
- Brent crude oil dropped 6.4% to $106.20 per barrel
- West Texas Intermediate fell 6.5% to $97.35 per barrel
This represents a pullback from the previous week when Brent crude topped $110 per barrel, marking its highest point since the start of the war.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio indicated the administration's preference for peaceful resolution, stating: "we would prefer to do it peacefully," while emphasizing military capability remains available if needed.
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi signaled openness to a peace agreement contingent on the United States demonstrating "goodwill."

According to the Islamic Republic News Agency, Iran is seeking: lift of U.S. sanctions; reduction of U.S. military presence in the region; removal of the blockade on the Strait of Hormuz.
Negotiators left Qatar on Sunday with the draft proposal, with follow-up meetings planned to finalize potential peace terms.
